clue.text: Room in which cleaner accepts award

indicators.note: a cleaner who accepts an award takes it inside herself, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a char is a cleaning lady, short for charwoman
the MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A room where the cleaning lady is being given an honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamber is a room, especially a bedroom or a formal meeting room.

clue.text: Grain that's planted before in California

indicators.note: planted means put in the ground, here set inside the state abbreviation
in marks the state abbreviation as the container

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A crop sown earlier in a Californian field.
explanation.definitionFit: A cereal is a grain crop such as wheat, barley or maize.

clue.text: Warrior that runs a long way

definitions.meaning: a woman warrior of Greek legend
a river runs, and this South American one is among the longest in the world

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the legendary tribe of female fighters and to the great river of South America.

parts.note: better means stronger, as in recovering health
a half is a half-pint of beer in a British pub

explanation.surface: A pub-goer asking a friend whether he wants a stronger beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mate' sounds like a pub friend, but it means a spouse; the question mark flags that.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's spouse or partner is jocularly called their other half in British English.

indicators.note: the woman consumes the letter, so it goes inside her name

parts.note: Rita is a woman's name
A is the abbreviation for ace in playing cards

explanation.surface: A woman eating the very best Indian food.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is an Indian side dish of yoghurt with cucumber or herbs.

clue.text: Extreme cold getting into kind of tyre

indicators.note: one piece getting into another sits inside it

parts.note: a radial is a type of car tyre with cords running across it
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Something very chilly working its way into a car tyre.
explanation.definitionFit: Radical and extreme are synonyms for views or measures that go far beyond the usual.

clue.text: Second course, perhaps, that will revive you

definitions.meaning: a course taken again to update skills learnt earlier
a drink or anything else that refreshes

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an update training course and something, such as a drink, that refreshes.

indicators.note: one letter entering a room goes inside it

parts.note: a den is a small private room
A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: A senior clergyman stepping forward into a room.
explanation.definitionFit: A dean is a senior cleric in charge of a cathedral.

clue.text: Agree company will get part that's covered in broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means sent out over the air, so the word is heard not written

parts.note: the inside of something is the part covered by its outside

explanation.surface: A firm agreeing to take a role in a radio show.
explanation.definitionFit: Opinions that coincide agree with one another.

clue.text: Ointment ruined linen mitt almost entirely

indicators.note: ruined suggests the letters are messed up and rearranged
almost entirely means all but the last letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: A rub-on lotion that spoilt a linen glove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost entirely' drops the final T from LINEN MITT, and 'ruined' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A liniment is a liquid rubbed onto the skin to ease aches, a kind of ointment.

definitions.meaning: to reply or behave in answer to something
split as ..., to act again, as a performer does when called back

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading: an encore is a performance repeated, so the word split after its first two letters means perform once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To react is to respond to a stimulus, and read as re-act it means perform a second time.

clue.text: Rising costs in Apartment No.1 overturned …

parts.note: taken as written
a flat is an apartment in British English

indicators.note: overturned says the abbreviation and the figure that follow it are read in the opposite order

parts.note: No is the abbreviation for number and 1 is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A complaint about the cost of living, trailing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' turns NO and I into I then ON. The ellipsis joins this clue to the next, which carries on the thought about finances.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflation is the general rise in prices over time, so rising costs describes it.

clue.text: … but a move to a houseboat would help one stay thus

definitions.text: but a move to a houseboat would help one stay thus

parts.words: but a move to a houseboat would help one stay thus
parts.note: following the previous clue about rising costs, the phrase means solvent, and a houseboat floats on a river, keeping its owner literally afloat

explanation.walkthrough: Read with the clue before it: in a time of rising prices you want to stay solvent, and living on a boat would keep you so in the most literal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping your head above water is the idiom for staying out of debt, and a houseboat literally floats.

indicators.note: reversible is a coat word here but signals that the coats are read back to front

parts.note: macs are raincoats, short for mackintoshes

explanation.surface: A con trick involving coats that can be worn either way out.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiddle is a swindle or dishonest scheme, which is just what a scam is.

definitions.meaning: relating to one single thing, specific

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both fastidious and specific to one thing, as in a particular case.

definitions.meaning: a long clay tobacco pipe of a traditional design
a lay officer of an Anglican parish who looks after church property

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a long-stemmed clay smoking pipe and an elected lay official of a parish church.

definitions.meaning: to sell off a book's unsold copies cheaply

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means sell surplus copies of a book cheaply; as a noun it means what is left.

clue.text: Media mingling in a cricket club — presenting 'The Don'?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go in the middle of the other pieces
mingling means mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Media folk mixing at a cricket club as if one were the great batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Don' suggests Don Bradman, the cricketer, given the cricket club; but a don is a university lecturer.
explanation.definitionFit: A don is a teacher at Oxford or Cambridge, so a university scholar.

definitions.meaning: examines in detail, as a verb
detailed itemised examinations, as a plural noun

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means examines closely; as a plural noun it means detailed itemisations.

clue.text: Industrial group needs answer to puncture awful recent gloom

indicators.note: the single letter is pushed through, so it sits inside the rearranged letters
awful suggests the letters are in a dreadful state and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A business conglomerate needing a solution to the recent gloomy mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges RECENT GLOOM to CONGLOMERTE, and 'to puncture' puts A inside it between R and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A conglomerate is a large corporation made of many different businesses, an industrial group.

clue.text: Knight maybe put on half of little cloak

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is put on top of the second

parts.note: a knight is an example of a man, a chess piece

indicators.note: half of takes the last three of the six letters

explanation.surface: A knight putting on a small cloak.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantle is a loose sleeveless cloak.

definitions.meaning: checks or halts growth, as a verb

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both halts growth and daring feats done to get noticed.

parts.note: to do someone is slang for cheating or swindling them
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: An insult hurled at an officer caught cheating.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolt is a stupid person, and blockhead is an old word for the same.

parts.note: a broomstick is the vehicle a witch flies on, so it is that witch's craft in the sense of a vessel

explanation.walkthrough: Craft means both a skill and a vehicle; a witch's broom is her flying craft, and the word for her magic arts also names it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorcery is the art of witches, and their traditional flying craft is a broom.

parts.note: Labour is a party of the political left

explanation.surface: Asking whether the two big British parties are divided.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleft means split or divided, as in a cleft chin.

parts.note: the TA was the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
a cricket team has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: The army cricket team travelling in its vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi is a hired car, a vehicle.

indicators.note: said signals that the word for girl is only heard, giving its sound not its spelling

parts.note: miss is a word for a young girl
a handle is slang for a person's name or title

explanation.surface: Accusing someone of mistreating a young woman who has a title.
explanation.definitionFit: To mishandle someone is to treat them roughly or badly, to maltreat them.

clue.text: Remember this language? The French can

parts.note: la is a French word for the
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A quiz asking whether you recall a language, with a French hint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remember this' teases those who learnt the language at school and have mostly forgotten it.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin is the language of ancient Rome, still taught in schools.

definitions.meaning: to dismiss someone from the armed forces in disgrace
a person at a checkout who takes payment

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means dismiss from military service; as a noun it is the checkout operator who handles money.

clue.text: Flipping routine — A, B, C and so on — that's for the birds

indicators.note: flipping means turned over, so the word for routine is read back to front

parts.note: a rut is a dull fixed routine

parts.words: A, B, C and so on
parts.note: A, B and C are musical keys

explanation.surface: Grumbling that the ABC routine is fit only for the birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' turns RUT into TUR; A, B and C are musical keys, not the alphabet's start. 'That's for the birds' is an idiom for something worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: Turkeys are large birds farmed for their meat.
